rules.title: Measure BB: 5% cap on Annual General Adjustment (AGA)
rules.requirement: The Rent Board sets the AGA by the CPI-based formula in the Rent Ordinance, but the AGA approved for any year cannot exceed 5%. The cap does not stop landlords with banked (unused) AGAs from raising rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.key_value: AGA = CPI-based formula, capped at 5%
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units
rules.exemptions: Cap does not prevent banked (unused) AGAs from previous years from being used to raise rent to the rent ceiling, even if the increase exceeds 5%.
rules.interaction: Banked AGAs may produce an increase greater than 5% up to the rent ceiling.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Measure BB: Annual inflation adjustment of owner move-in eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: The Rent Board must adjust owner move-in eviction relocation assistance payment amounts for inflation every year.
rules.key_value: Annual inflationary adjustment of OMI relocation assistance
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.

rules.title: Security deposit cap (state AB 12): one month's rent
rules.requirement: Since July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit for furnished and unfurnished units. Last month's rent counts toward the deposit; first month's rent does not.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to furnished and unfurnished units; landlords not meeting the small-landlord criteria.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords (see BERK-DEP-02) may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.interaction: Last month's rent is considered part of the security deposit; first month's rent is not. Before July 1, 2024 the cap was two months (unfurnished) / three months (furnished).
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (AB 12), as described by Berkeley Rent Board
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Small landlord exception: two months' rent deposit
rules.requirement: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units, if owned by a natural person, family trust, or an LLC whose members are all natural persons.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord owns only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total; ownership by natural person, family trust, or LLC with all natural-person members.
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (AB 12), as described by Berkeley Rent Board
rules.quoted_span: landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units

rules.title: Photograph unit at start of tenancy
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document its condition.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy

rules.title: Move-out walk-through inspection
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy so tenants can fix issues to avoid deposit deductions.
rules.quoted_span: landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning

rules.title: Permitted security deposit deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary to cover rent default, repair tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, clean the unit to its move-in level of cleanliness, and, if the lease allows, restore or replace personal property or furniture. Professional cleaning cannot be required unless reasonably necessary to restore move-in condition.
rules.coverage_conditions: Cleaning deduction applies to tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to:

rules.title: Return of deposit within 21 days with itemized statement
rules.requirement: The remaining deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates. If deductions are made, the landlord must provide an itemized written statement with copies of documents showing charges; from Jan 1, 2025 proof that repairs were completed; and from April 1, 2025, after-possession photos and a written cost explanation.
rules.key_value: 21 days
rules.quoted_span: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned

rules.title: Security deposit interest under Berkeley Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year

rules.title: Prohibition on use of algorithmic devices to set or recommend rents
rules.requirement: Landlords and property management companies in Cambridge may not use, subscribe to, or employ an algorithmic device (software, AI, or automated data system using non-public or aggregated competitor data) to set, adjust, determine, or recommend residential rental pricing or unit occupancy levels.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting tools
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords (owners, managers, lessors of residential real property) and property management companies operating in Cambridge
rules.exemptions: Single-family residential properties where the owner resides on the premises; housing owned or operated by a public housing authority or higher education institution for student housing (§ 8.75.040).
rules.interaction: Penalty: $1,000 per residential unit per month of violation; City Solicitor may seek injunctive relief (§ 8.75.050).
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for any landlord or property management company operating in the City of Cambridge to use, subscribe to, or employ an algorithmic device to set, adjust, determine, or recommend residential rental pricing or unit occupancy levels.

rules.title: Prohibition on sharing non-public pricing/occupancy data for rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not enter into agreements or arrangements with other housing providers or algorithmic pricing intermediaries to share non-public occupancy, pricing, or lease renewal data for rent coordination purposes.
rules.key_value: Ban on data-sharing for rent coordination
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords operating in Cambridge
rules.exemptions: Single-family residential properties where the owner resides on the premises; housing owned or operated by a public housing authority or higher education institution for student housing (§ 8.75.040).
rules.interaction: Penalty: $1,000 per residential unit per month of violation (§ 8.75.050).
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall enter into an agreement or arrangement with other housing providers or algorithmic pricing intermediaries to share non-public occupancy, pricing, or lease renewal data for rent coordination purposes.

rules.title: Prohibition on sale or provision of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale/licensing of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; algorithms using non-public Competitor Data less than 90 days old.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated/anonymous published rental data reports that make no recommendations; affordable housing rent/income limit products; market research for project financing, appraisals, and software research/testing/training (if Competitor Data not used as live input).
rules.interaction: Ordinance 7,992-N.S. amends Chapter 13.63; does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley. Each month of violation and each unit for which the algorithm was used is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Per-month, per-unit separate violations
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Same exclusions as the definition of coordinated pricing algorithm in § 13.63.020(A).
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described

rules.title: Definition of coordinated pricing algorithm and Competitor Data
rules.requirement: A coordinated pricing algorithm is any process that uses non-public Competitor Data to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and competitors, including via a third-party vendor. Competitor Data is non-public data on other landlords' properties less than 90 days old.
rules.key_value: Competitor Data < 90 days old
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to recommendations for future leases by City of Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: (a) aggregated, anonymous published rental data without recommendations; (b) products establishing rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; (c) market research for project financing, appraisal, or research/testing/training for software development.
rules.quoted_span: uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or

rules.title: City Attorney enforcement and penalties
rules.requirement: The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing City Attorney recovers attorney's fees and costs.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Violations of § 13.63.030(A) and/or (B).
rules.quoted_span: The City Attorney may file a civil action for violations of section 13.63.030,

rules.title: Tenant private right of action
rules.requirement: An aggrieved tenant may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation of the landlord-use prohibition; a prevailing tenant is awarded attorney's fees and costs, and lease provisions limiting such fees are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Violations of § 13.63.030(B) (landlord use).
rules.quoted_span: An aggrieved tenant may file a civil action for violations of section 13.63.030,

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing: prohibition on criminal history inquiry and use
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. Prohibited acts include inquiring, stating that persons with criminal backgrounds won't be considered, refusing to rent or terminating a tenancy, requiring disclosure, demanding higher deposit or rent, refusing to add a family member, disqualifying from rental assistance programs, or otherwise treating applicants/tenants differently based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiry or use in tenant selection
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to current and prospective tenants of rental housing providers in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) where an owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making

rules.title: Written notice and opportunity to respond before adverse action based on criminal history
rules.requirement: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, the landlord must give the applicant/tenant written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Written notice + opportunity to respond
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the ordinance generally (lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8, owner-occupied 1-3 unit, etc.).
rules.quoted_span: the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond

rules.title: Fair Chance notice posting requirement
rules.requirement: Housing providers must prominently include the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants on application materials, websites, and at locations they control that applicants frequently visit.
rules.key_value: Notice on applications, websites, and frequently visited locations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers must include the following Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants prominently on their application materials, websites, and at any locations under their control that are frequently visited by Applicants

rules.title: Penalties for Fair Chance Ordinance violations
rules.requirement: Violators face administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, civil damages (actual damages or three times one month's rent), punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.key_value: $1,000–$10,000 per violation; 3x monthly rent damages
rules.quoted_span: administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent

rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee (state cap, 2026)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a tenant screening fee of no more than the state-set maximum, $68.96 for 2026. The fee may be used to obtain information such as a consumer credit report, and the applicant must receive a copy of the report, a receipt with itemized costs, and a refund of any unused portion.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is

rules.title: No screening fee if no unit available; refund or first-qualified-applicant policy
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must return the fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy of reviewing applications in order received (first qualified applicant gets the unit) and not charging a fee to any applicant not considered.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Landlord must use reusable screening report
rules.requirement: If the prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights disclosure (BMC 13.78.010)
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and process an application must provide, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code 1950.6(b).
rules.interaction: Implements state fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
rules.requirement: Owners cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate.
rules.quoted_span: cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy

rules.title: Chapter 13.78 applies to existing rental agreements (BMC 13.78.018)
rules.requirement: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary contract language; lease provisions that violate the chapter are unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary.

rules.title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 amounts)
rules.requirement: Owners who evict a tenant for an owner move-in must pay relocation assistance. Effective January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, with an additional $6,471 for qualifying households. Amounts are adjusted yearly by CPI.
rules.key_value: $19,413 standard + $6,471 additional for qualifying households (2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owner move-in evictions under the Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; additional payment applies to qualifying households.
rules.interaction: Indexed annually to the 12-month CPI-U change for the San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose region (1.5% for 2026); Rent Board approved Oct 16, 2025.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Rent Board 2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

rules.title: Ellis Act eviction relocation assistance (2026 amounts)
rules.requirement: Owners withdrawing a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions. For 2026 this is $19,413 standard plus $6,471 additional for qualifying households.
rules.key_value: $19,413 standard + $6,471 additional for qualifying households (2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act).
rules.interaction: Payments mirror owner move-in relocation amounts and are indexed annually to CPI-U for the San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose region.
rules.citation: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance; Rent Board 2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments
rules.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) of 1.0%
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026. The AGA is set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase for July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025 (1.5%).
rules.coverage_conditions: Eligible landlords of units subject to Berkeley rent stabilization that meet the conditions in Regulation 1148; notice to tenants required.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set pursuant to Costa-Hawkins are not adjusted by the 2026 AGA.
rules.interaction: Interacts with the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act regarding initial rent setting for new tenancies.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span: allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026

rules.title: AGA exclusion for post-2025 Costa-Hawkins tenancies
rules.requirement: The 2026 AGA cannot be used to adjust rent for tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins.
rules.key_value: No 2026 AGA for tenancies beginning on/after 2025-01-01 with Costa-Hawkins rents
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set pursuant to Costa-Hawkins.
rules.interaction: Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
rules.citation: Rent Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A
rules.quoted_span:
The 2026 AGA may not adjust tenants’ rents when their tenancy began on or after
January 1, 2025, and who had their rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental
Housing Act.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance: No blanket ban on arrests/convictions; case-by-case review
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not impose a blanket policy denying housing to anyone with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants case-by-case.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history ban; case-by-case review
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; does not apply to current criminal behavior
rules.interaction: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal history requirement preempts this policy.
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017), preamble
rules.quoted_span: will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance: Prohibited criminal-history categories (arrests, relief, juvenile, >5 years)
rules.requirement: Agents may not consider arrests not resulting in conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when determining eligibility or considering eviction.
rules.key_value: 5-year conviction lookback; no non-conviction arrests, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units
rules.exemptions: Not applicable where direct relationship between conviction and housing sought or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to safety of others; not applicable to current criminal behavior
rules.interaction: Federal or state law criminal history requirements preempt conflicting provisions.
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017), § 1(a)-(d)
rules.quoted_span: A conviction more than 5 years old.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance: Credit score may not be used; credit history limited
rules.requirement: Agents may not use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny applications. Credit history may only be used in lieu of rental history when rental history is unavailable, and lack of credit history alone is not sufficient to reject an applicant.
rules.key_value: No credit score use
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017), Credit § 5(a)-(c)
rules.quoted_span: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing

rules.title: Rental assistance (Section 8 voucher) source-of-income discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters based on rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is treated as housing discrimination.
rules.key_value: Rental assistance is a protected class
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to renting, buying, selling, or financing of any housing in the City of Boston; no unit-count or year-built cutoffs stated.
rules.interaction: Enforced alongside local, state, and federal fair housing laws.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Commission, Boston Fair Housing Regulations (boston.gov)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy (eviction or lease non-renewal) must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources to the tenant at the same time as the Notice to Quit. This is a procedural notice duty and does not itself require just cause.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with Notice to Quit / non-renewal
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Requirements cannot be waived; lease terms purporting to waive them are void. Violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span: In the event that your landlord serves you with a Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease

rules.title: HSNA – Copy of Notice to Quit/Non-renewal to Office of Housing Stability
rules.requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners must send the City's Office of Housing Stability a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease, together with a Certificate of Compliance/Service.
rules.key_value: Copy of notice + Certificate of Compliance/Service to Office of Housing Stability
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.citation: Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span: The HSNA also requires landlords and foreclosing owners to send a copy of the

rules.title: HSNA – Enforcement and penalties
rules.requirement: Violations are investigated by the Office of Fair Housing and Equity and enforced by Inspectional Services Department: warning for first offense, $300 per day for second and subsequent offenses. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.key_value: Warning; then $300 per day
rules.interaction: If a landlord violates the HSNA, it does not halt the eviction process.
rules.quoted_span: 2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day

rules.title: Source of income / Section 8 voucher discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent to a tenant because they hold a Section 8 voucher, and must comply with rental assistance program requirements (completing forms, signing documents, allowing inspections). Source of income, including government rental assistance, is a protected characteristic.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is protected
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords, property managers, tenant screening companies, and other housing providers covering most housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics; shared living area single-sex housing; senior housing may be limited by age.
rules.quoted_span: Refusing to rent to a tenant with a section 8 voucher.

rules.title: Criminal history screening protections
rules.requirement: FEHA provides specific protections for people with criminal histories searching for housing; blanket refusals to rent to anyone with a criminal history may be discriminatory.
rules.key_value: Blanket criminal history bans may be discriminatory
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers and tenant screening companies under FEHA.
rules.quoted_span: Refusing to rent to anyone with a criminal history

rules.title: Discriminatory tenant screening prohibited, including by third parties
rules.requirement: Screening prospective tenants, including through a third-party tenant screening company, in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic is unlawful.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic

rules.title: No higher security deposit for households with children
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not impose conditions such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children, which is familial status discrimination.
rules.key_value: Same security deposit regardless of familial status
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most housing providers under FEHA.
rules.exemptions: Qualifying senior housing may exclude people based on age, including families with children.
rules.quoted_span: such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not impose blanket bans. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant and not a threat to the health and safety of others or property, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; convictions must be directly related to tenancy risk
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers in California generally
rules.interaction: Local ordinances may add further limits
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, rental assistance, SSI/SSDI, or wages. Refusing to comply with subsidy program paperwork and advertising such as "No Section 8" are also prohibited.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers in California generally
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent

rules.title: No higher security deposit based on source of income
rules.requirement: Charging a higher security deposit to applicants because they use Section 8 or other rental assistance is unlawful source of income discrimination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applicants or tenants using Section 8 or other rental assistance
rules.interaction: Example of source of income discrimination (CA-SCREEN-02)
rules.quoted_span: charging a higher security deposit for Section 8 applicants

rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service animals and ESAs
rules.requirement: Tenants with service animals or emotional support animals, kept as reasonable accommodations, cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them, and breed, size, or weight restrictions do not apply.
rules.key_value: $0 pet deposit / pet rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Service animals and ESAs of persons with disabilities
rules.interaction: AB 468 (2021) does not change housing rights for ESAs
rules.quoted_span: tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them

rules.title: Criminal conviction must be directly related; consider nature, severity, and time elapsed
rules.requirement: When assessing whether an applicant's criminal conviction is directly related to a legitimate housing interest, a housing provider should consider the nature and severity of the crime and how much time has passed since the criminal conduct.
rules.key_value: Consider nature/severity of crime and time elapsed
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers using criminal conviction history in housing decisions; the excerpt begins mid-passage, so the full coverage conditions are not shown.
rules.interaction: Operates under FEHA; see CRD's Fair Housing and Criminal History factsheet and FAQ for details.
rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq. (FEHA); CRD Fair Housing and Criminal History guidance
rules.quoted_span: a housing provider should consider the nature and severity of the crime and the amount of time that has passed since the criminal conduct occurred.

rules.title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of an anticompetitive agreement
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. The rule is not limited to housing, so it reaches rent-setting software.
rules.key_value: Common pricing algorithm use/distribution within a conspiracy is unlawful
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702, excluding end consumers. 'Distribute' includes selling, licensing, providing access to, or otherwise making available, including by subscription. 'Price' includes any amount of money or other thing of value expected, required, or given in payment for any product or service. The text does not name housing or rent specifically.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not 'persons' under the statute.
rules.interaction: Section 16729(c) provides that the section does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws (the Cartwright Act). Section 16756.1, added by the same bill, sets a lenient pleading standard for Cartwright Act complaints.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Ban on coercing adoption of common pricing algorithm recommendations
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt the price or commercial term the algorithm recommends for the same or similar products or services in California. This applies even without a proven conspiracy.
rules.key_value: Coercing adoption of algorithmic price or commercial term recommendations is unlawful
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702. 'Commercial term' includes level of service, availability, and output. The text does not name housing or rent specifically.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not 'persons' under the statute.
rules.interaction: Section 16729(c) provides that the section does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: Substantial remodel/demolition termination notice content
rules.requirement: A notice terminating a tenancy for demolition or substantial remodel must describe the intent, the remodel scope and duration (or demolition date), include a copy of permits (or a signed contractor contract for hazardous-materials abatement without permits), include the re-rent offer statement, and notify the tenant to share contact info if interested in reoccupying.
rules.key_value: Notice must include permits/contract and re-rent statement
rules.quoted_span: A written notice terminating a tenancy for a just cause pursuant to this subparagraph shall include all of the following information:

rules.title: Notice and opportunity to cure for curable lease violations
rules.requirement: Before terminating for a curable lease violation, the owner must first give notice with an opportunity to cure under CCP § 1161(3). If not cured in the stated period, a three-day notice to quit without opportunity to cure may be served.
rules.key_value: Cure notice before three-day notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: the owner shall first give notice of the violation to the tenant with an opportunity to cure the violation pursuant to paragraph (3) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause
rules.requirement: For no-fault just cause terminations, the owner must, regardless of tenant income, either pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, equal to one month of rent in effect when notice was issued. Payment must be made within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, and the notice must inform the tenant of this right. Failure to strictly comply voids the notice.
rules.key_value: 1 month rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies requiring just cause under subdivision (a), no-fault just cause under (b)(2)
rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.

rules.title: Exemptions from just cause requirements
rules.requirement: The statute does not apply to transient/tourist hotels, certain institutional housing, dormitories, owner-shared housing, certain owner-occupied residences, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable property with non-corporate/non-REIT owners and proper notice, and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.key_value: 15-year rolling certificate of occupancy exemption
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years
rules.exemptions: Hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner; owner-occupied single-family (up to two units/bedrooms rented); owner-occupied duplex; separately alienable property with non-REIT/corporation/LLC-with-corporate-member owner and written exemption notice; affordable housing
rules.quoted_span:
Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15
years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.

rules.title: Required notice of rights to tenants
rules.requirement: Owners must give tenants notice of rent cap and just cause protections in the lease, addendum, or signed written notice, in at least 12-point type, with the statutory language.
rules.key_value: 12-point type notice
rules.quoted_span: The notification or lease provision shall be in no less than 12-point type

rules.title: Remedies and voiding of notice for violations
rules.requirement: Failure to comply with any provision voids the termination notice. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, possible attorney's fees, and up to treble damages if willful, and the AG, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.key_value: Up to 3x actual damages
rules.quoted_span: An owner’s failure to comply with any provision of this section shall render the

rules.title: Local just cause ordinance preemption
rules.requirement: The state just cause statute does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 applies, or one adopted or amended after that date that is more protective.
rules.coverage_conditions: Local ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or later and more protective
rules.quoted_span: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.
rules.conflict_note: Local ordinances may supersede state law; text truncated before full 'more protective' criteria.

rules.title: Local just cause ordinances adopted on or before Sept. 1, 2019 displace state law
rules.requirement: Residential property covered by a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 is exempt from the state just cause statute, and the local ordinance applies instead.
rules.key_value: Local ordinance (adopted on or before 9/1/2019) applies instead of § 1946.2
rules.coverage_conditions: Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019
rules.exemptions: Property is exempt from § 1946.2 because the local ordinance governs
overrides: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (state just cause) as applied to properties covered by earlier local ordinances
rules.interaction: Property is never subject to both the local ordinance and § 1946.2 (see (i)(2)).
rules.quoted_span: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.title: More protective local ordinances adopted or amended after Sept. 1, 2019 apply instead of state law
rules.requirement: A local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019 displaces the state statute only if it is more protective. This means it is consistent with the state statute, further limits termination reasons, provides higher relocation assistance, or adds other lawful protections, and the local government has made a binding finding in the ordinance that it is more protective.
rules.key_value: Three-part 'more protective' test, including a binding local finding
rules.coverage_conditions: Local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019
rules.exemptions: Property is exempt from § 1946.2 if the ordinance meets all three criteria
overrides: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (state just cause) as applied to properties covered by qualifying local ordinances
rules.interaction: Property is never subject to both the local ordinance and § 1946.2 (see (i)(2)).
rules.quoted_span: The local government has made a binding finding within their local ordinance that the ordinance is more protective than the provisions of this section.

rules.title: Less protective post-2019 local ordinances not enforceable; no dual coverage
rules.requirement: A property cannot be subject to both a local just cause ordinance and the state statute. A local ordinance adopted after September 1, 2019 that is less protective than the state statute cannot be enforced unless the state statute is repealed.
rules.key_value: Less protective local ordinances (post-9/1/2019) unenforceable
rules.coverage_conditions: Local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 that are less protective than § 1946.2
overrides: Less protective local just cause ordinances adopted after 2019-09-01
rules.interaction: The state statute is repealed on January 1, 2030 under subsection (n), which would lift the bar on enforcing less protective local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: A residential real property shall not be subject to both a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy and this section.

rules.title: Waiver of state just cause rights is void
rules.requirement: Any waiver by a tenant of rights under the state just cause statute is void as contrary to public policy.
rules.key_value: Waivers void
rules.quoted_span: Any waiver of the rights under this section shall be void as contrary to public policy.

rules.title: Mobilehome owners excluded; operative date and sunset of state just cause statute
rules.requirement: The state just cause statute does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Section 798.9. It became operative on April 1, 2024 and is repealed on January 1, 2030 unless extended.
rules.key_value: Operative 2024-04-01; repealed 2030-01-01
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including units in a mobilehome park
rules.exemptions: Homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9
rules.quoted_span: This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

rules.title: Mobilehome tenancy rent cap applies to increases on or after Feb 18, 2021
rules.requirement: The statewide rent increase cap in subdivision (a) applies to mobilehome tenancies only for rent increases occurring on or after February 18, 2021.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in a mobilehome subject to subdivision (a); increases on/after 2021-02-18
rules.exemptions: Homeowners of a mobilehome as defined in Civ. Code § 798.9 (subd. (j))
rules.quoted_span: only to rent increases for a tenancy in a mobilehome subject to subdivision (a) occurring on or after February 18, 2021.

rules.title: Mobilehome excess increases Feb 18, 2021–Jan 1, 2022 reset; no overpayment liability
rules.requirement: If an owner raised mobilehome rent above the permitted amount between Feb 18, 2021 and Jan 1, 2022, the applicable rent on Jan 1, 2022 is the Feb 18, 2021 rent plus the maximum permissible increase. The owner is not liable to the tenant for corresponding overpayment.
rules.coverage_conditions: Mobilehome tenancies; increases between 2021-02-18 and 2022-01-01 exceeding subdivision (a) limit
rules.quoted_span: An owner shall not be liable to the tenant for any corresponding rent overpayment.

rules.title: Two-step increase allowance for under-cap increases (Feb 18, 2021–Jan 1, 2022)
rules.requirement: An owner who raised rent between Feb 18, 2021 and Jan 1, 2022 by less than the permitted amount may increase rent twice within 12 months of Feb 18, 2021, but the total may not exceed the maximum permitted by subdivision (a).
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property subject to subdivision (a); prior increase on/after 2021-02-18 and before 2022-01-01 below the cap
rules.quoted_span: shall be allowed to increase the rental rate twice, as provided in paragraph (2) of subdivision (a), within 12 months of February 18, 2021

rules.title: Mobilehome homeowners excluded from rent cap
rules.requirement: The statewide rent cap does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Civ. Code § 798.9.
rules.exemptions: Homeowners of a mobilehome (Civ. Code § 798.9)
rules.quoted_span: This section shall not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9.

rules.title: Civil liability and enforcement for excess rent
rules.requirement: An owner who demands or collects rent above the maximum allowed is liable to the tenant for injunctive relief, excess amounts, discretionary attorney's fees, and up to treble damages if willful or malicious. The AG, city attorney or county counsel may enforce; actions must be brought within three years.
rules.key_value: Excess rent damages; up to 3x if willful; 3-year limitation
rules.quoted_span: An owner who demands, accepts, receives, or retains any payment of rent in excess of the maximum rent allowed by this section shall be liable in a civil action to the tenant

rules.title: Waiver of rent cap rights void
rules.requirement: Any waiver of tenant rights under the statewide rent cap statute is void as contrary to public policy.
rules.quoted_span: Any waiver of the rights under this section shall be void as contrary to public policy.

rules.title: No expansion or limitation of local rent control authority
rules.requirement: The statewide cap does not authorize local governments to set limits not otherwise permissible under Civ. Code Ch. 2.7 (Costa-Hawkins) nor affect their existing authority to adopt or maintain rent controls consistent with that chapter.
rules.interaction: Local rent control consistent with Civ. Code § 1954.50 et seq. remains unaffected
rules.quoted_span: Nothing in this section authorizes a local government to establish limitations on any rental rate increases not otherwise permissible under Chapter 2.7

rules.title: Operative date and sunset of rent cap statute (SB 567 version)
rules.requirement: This version of § 1947.12 became operative April 1, 2024 and remains in effect until January 1, 2030, when it is repealed.
rules.key_value: Operative 2024-04-01; repealed 2030-01-01
rules.quoted_span: This section shall remain in effect until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

rules.title: Security deposit cap: one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however denominated, exceeding one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent paid on or before initial occupancy. Applies to residential dwelling rental agreements.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected on or after July 1, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent if lease term is six months or longer; mutual agreement for tenant-requested alterations; small-landlord two-month cap under (c)(5).
rules.interaction: Small landlord exception in (c)(5) raises cap to two months, but not for service members.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent

rules.title: Small landlord two-month security cap
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units total, may not demand or receive more than two months' rent as security.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord is a natural person (including settlor/beneficiary of family trust) or LLC with all natural person members; owns no more than two residential rental properties collectively with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member; landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of this.
rules.quoted_span: in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements

rules.title: Higher security for service members: disclosure and return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard or advertised security due to credit or housing history or other tenant factor, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason before lease signing. The additional amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.key_value: Return of additional security after 6 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Service member as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400.
rules.quoted_span: The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant

rules.title: Initial inspection and itemized statement
rules.requirement: Landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the right to request an initial inspection, conduct it on request no earlier than two weeks before termination with 48 hours' written notice, and give an itemized statement of proposed deductions; tenant may cure deficiencies before termination.
rules.key_value: 48 hours' written notice of inspection
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when tenancy is terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3), or (4); duties discharged if tenant does not request an inspection.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall give the tenant an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleanings that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the security

rules.title: Security held for tenant; priority over creditors
rules.requirement: Any security must be held by the landlord for the tenant, and the tenant's claim to it is prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: The claim of a tenant to the security shall be prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord.

rules.title: Photographs of unit at tenancy inception
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the inception of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.title: Landlord photographs at move-out and after repairs/cleaning
rules.requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit within a reasonable time after possession is returned and before repairs or cleanings that will be deducted from the deposit, and again after those repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.key_value: Photographs before and after repairs/cleaning
rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord

rules.title: 21-day itemized statement and return of deposit
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any deductions and return any remaining deposit.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises

rules.title: Electronic return of deposit
rules.requirement: If the landlord received the security or rent electronically, the remainder must be returned electronically to the tenant's designated account or by an agreed method, and the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of this right.
rules.exemptions: Notice requirement does not apply where parties previously agreed in writing on another method or tenancy terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord received the security or rental payments from the tenant electronically, the landlord shall return the remainder of the security electronically

rules.title: Multiple adult tenants: joint check
rules.requirement: Where multiple adult tenants reside in the unit, absent a written mutual agreement, the landlord must return the deposit by check payable to all adult tenants and send the itemized statement to any one of them.
rules.exemptions: Written mutual agreement among landlord and all adult tenants; tenant terminating under Section 1946.7 may request other disbursement.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall return the remainder of the security by a check made payable to all adult tenants on the rental or lease agreement

rules.title: Documentation of repair and cleaning deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must include with the itemized statement copies of documents showing charges for repair or cleaning (bills, invoices, receipts, or description of work with time and hourly rate), plus photographs taken under subdivision (g).
rules.quoted_span: If a deduction is made for repairs or cleanings allowed by this section, the landlord shall provide photographs taken pursuant to subdivision (g)

rules.title: Good faith estimate when work or documents not complete
rules.requirement: If repairs cannot be completed or documents are unavailable within 21 days, the landlord may deduct a good faith estimate and must complete documentation within 14 calendar days of completing the repair or receiving documentation.
rules.key_value: 14 calendar days to complete
rules.quoted_span: the landlord may deduct the amount of a good faith estimate of the charges that will be incurred and provide that estimate with the itemized statement

rules.title: $125 documentation exemption and waiver; tenant request
rules.requirement: Landlord need not provide documentation if deductions for repairs and cleaning total $125 or less or the tenant validly waived, but must comply if the tenant requests documentation within 14 days of receiving the itemized statement; landlord then has 14 days to comply.
rules.exemptions: Tenant waiver signed at or after notice of termination or no earlier than 60 days before fixed-term lease expiration.
rules.quoted_span: The deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125).

rules.title: Forfeiture for bad faith noncompliance
rules.requirement: The landlord cannot claim any amount of the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with the return and itemization subdivision.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not be entitled to claim any amount of the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with this

rules.title: Deposit upon termination of landlord's interest
rules.requirement: Upon sale, assignment, death, receivership or other termination of the landlord's interest, the landlord must within a reasonable time transfer the remaining deposit to the successor and notify the tenant, or return it to the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: Upon termination of the landlord’s interest in the premises, whether by sale, assignment, death, appointment of receiver, or otherwise

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor landlord
rules.requirement: On transfer of the landlord's interest, the landlord must either transfer the remaining deposit (after lawful deductions) to the successor and notify the tenant, or return it to the tenant with an accounting. Before a voluntary transfer, the landlord must give the successor a written statement of the remaining security, itemized deductions, and the landlord's election.
rules.key_value: Notice to tenant by personal delivery or first-class mail
rules.quoted_span: Transfer the portion of the security remaining after any lawful deductions are made under subdivision (e) to the landlord’s successor in interest.

rules.title: Successor in interest joint and several liability
rules.requirement: If the landlord fails to comply with the transfer/return requirements, successors are jointly and severally liable for repayment of the deposit owed. A successor may not require a replacement deposit until it makes restitution or provides an accounting. A successor with a good faith belief after reasonable investigation that the deposit was transferred or returned is not liable for bad-faith damages or untransferred security.
rules.key_value: Joint and several liability
rules.exemptions: Successor with good faith belief after inquiry and reasonable investigation (subd. (k)(3))
rules.quoted_span: the landlord’s successors in interest shall be jointly and severally liable with the landlord for repayment of the security

rules.title: Bad faith retention of deposit - statutory damages
rules.requirement: Bad faith claim or retention of a deposit, or bad faith demand for replacement security, may subject the landlord or successor to statutory damages of up to twice the deposit plus actual damages. The landlord bears the burden of proof on the reasonableness of amounts claimed.
rules.key_value: Up to 2x deposit in statutory damages
rules.quoted_span: may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages

rules.title: No 'nonrefundable' deposit provisions
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not contain a provision characterizing any security as nonrefundable.
rules.key_value: Nonrefundable deposits prohibited
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Small claims and proof of deposit
rules.requirement: Deposit actions may be brought in small claims court within jurisdictional limits, and the existence and amount of a deposit may be proven by any credible evidence.
rules.quoted_span: Proof of the existence of and the amount of a security

rules.title: Application screening fee limited to actual costs and $30 cap (CPI-adjustable)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs and the reasonable value of time spent gathering applicant information. The fee may never exceed $30 per applicant, adjustable annually for CPI increases since January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted from 1998)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors/cosigners, for residential rental units.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt rules on deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs (subd. (l)).
overrides: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (as to screening fees)
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5; screening fee is not considered 'security' under 1950.5 or an 'advance fee' under B&P Code 10026.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Screening fee may not exceed actual out-of-pocket costs
rules.requirement: The fee amount must not exceed the actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering applicant information, including screening service or credit report costs, plus the reasonable value of the landlord's time.
rules.key_value: Actual costs, max $30 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applicants.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is or will be available within a reasonable time.
rules.key_value: No fee if no unit available
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applicants.
rules.quoted_span: shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Conditions for charging fee: first-come-first-served process or full refund process
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a fee only if, when collecting it, they offer either (A) a first-complete-application, written-criteria screening process where the first qualified applicant is approved and applicants are not charged unless their application is actually considered (with refund within seven days for inadvertent concurrent collections), or (B) a process returning the entire fee to any applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever first (option B); 7-day refund for inadvertent collection (option A)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applicants.
rules.exemptions: No refund required under option A where an application is denied after consideration for failing established screening criteria.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

rules.title: Itemized receipt for screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must give the applicant a receipt, personally or by mail (or email if agreed), itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information.
rules.key_value: Itemized receipt
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applicants who paid a fee.
rules.quoted_span: which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

rules.title: Refund of unused screening fee amounts
rules.requirement: If the landlord does not perform a personal reference check or obtain a consumer credit report, any portion of the fee not used for authorized purposes must be returned to the applicant.
rules.key_value: Return unused portion
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applicants who paid a fee.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord or their agent shall return any amount of the screening fee that is not used for the purposes authorized by this section to the applicant.

rules.title: Copy of consumer credit report to applicant within seven days
rules.requirement: If the applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must deliver a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: 7 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Applicants who paid a screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days

rules.title: Landlord may, but need not, accept applicant-provided credit report or reusable screening report
rules.requirement: A landlord may but is not required to accept and rely on a consumer credit report presented by an applicant, and may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental applications.
rules.interaction: Reusable screening reports are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.1.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may, but is not required to, accept and rely upon a consumer credit report presented by an applicant.

rules.title: Source of income and protected-class discrimination by housing owners
rules.requirement: Owners of housing accommodations may not discriminate against or harass any person based on protected characteristics, including source of income, veteran or military status, and others listed in the statute. rules.key_value: Source of income is a protected class

rules.requirement: Owners may not make or cause to be made written or oral inquiries about protected characteristics (e.g., race, religion, sex, familial status, disability, veteran status) of anyone seeking to rent or lease. Source of income is not in the list of barred inquiries.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations; applies to persons seeking to purchase, rent, or lease
rules.interaction: Subdivision (p)(2) permits inquiries about the level or source of income.
rules.quoted_span: make or to cause to be made any written or oral inquiry concerning the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of any person

rules.title: Aggregate income of co-residents must be counted like married persons
rules.requirement: A financial or income standard in rental housing must account for the aggregate income of persons residing or proposing to reside together on the same basis as married persons.

rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a landlord may not use a financial or income standard for eligibility that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.coverage_conditions: Instances in which there is a government rent subsidy
rules.exemptions: Does not limit the ability to request information or documentation to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (§ 12955(o)(2)).
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: Alternative evidence option when credit history used for subsidized tenancies
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a landlord using credit history in the application must offer the applicant the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay their portion of rent. If the applicant elects this, the landlord must give reasonable time to respond and reasonably consider the evidence in lieu of credit history.
rules.key_value: Alternative evidence in lieu of credit history
rules.coverage_conditions: Instances in which there is a government rent subsidy
rules.exemptions: Does not limit the ability to request information or documentation to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (§ 12955(o)(2)).

rules.title: Statewide prohibition on rent control
rules.requirement: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except for a narrow, voluntary, municipally compensated regime available to a municipality that accepts Chapter 40P.
rules.key_value: Rent control prohibited
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Cities or towns that accept Chapter 40P may adopt rent control meeting the conditions in clauses (a)-(c).
overrides: Local rent control ordinances or bylaws
rules.interaction: Preempts municipal rent control; the exception in § 4(a)-(c) is limited to voluntary, compensated regulation.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

rules.title: Conditions on permitted local rent control (voluntary, limited scope, compensation)
rules.requirement: A municipality accepting Chapter 40P may adopt rent control only if, after six months, owner compliance is entirely voluntary. The regulation may not cover occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or removal of properties, and the municipality must compensate owners from general funds for the difference between fair market rent and the controlled rent.
rules.key_value: Voluntary compliance after 6 months; owners compensated for difference between fair market rent and controlled rent; units with fair market rent over $400 excluded
rules.coverage_conditions: Only in municipalities that accept Chapter 40P; applies only to units of owners with ten or more rental units and fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.exemptions: Units owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units; units with fair market rent exceeding $400; owners declining to participate after six months.
rules.interaction: Regulation may not regulate evictions, so it does not create just-cause eviction protections.
rules.quoted_span: nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400

rules.title: Prohibition on refusing to rent based on protected characteristics
rules.requirement: Owners, lessees, brokers, managing agents and similar persons controlling publicly assisted or multiple dwellings or contiguously located housing may not refuse to rent or lease, or discriminate in terms, conditions or privileges, because of race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, veteran or armed forces status, or handicap (including blindness, hearing impairment, or use of a trained dog guide).
rules.key_value: Protected-class discrimination in renting prohibited
rules.coverage_conditions: Publicly assisted or multiple dwelling or contiguously located housing accommodations; subsection 7 (cut off in this text) covers other housing accommodations. Accessibility design/construction requirements apply to dwellings with three or more units first occupied after March 13, 1991 (all units if elevator building; ground floor units otherwise).
rules.exemptions: 'Age' protection does not apply to minors, state- or federally-aided elderly housing, LIHTC housing for persons 55+ or 62+, or 55+/62+ communities whose owner or manager registers biennially with the executive office of housing and livable communities; such housing must comply with 42 USC 3601 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: to refuse to rent or lease or sell or negotiate for sale or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons such accommodations because of the race

rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory inquiries of rental applicants
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not make or cause to be made any written or oral inquiry or record about an applicant's race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, veteran or armed forces status, blindness, hearing impairment or other handicap.
rules.key_value: No inquiries into protected characteristics
rules.coverage_conditions: Publicly assisted or multiple dwelling or contiguously located housing accommodations, and persons with right to rent, lease or sell them.
rules.exemptions: 'Age' does not apply to minors or to qualifying 55+/62+ housing as described in the subsection.
rules.quoted_span: to cause to be made any written or oral inquiry or record concerning the race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation

rules.title: Prohibition on refusing to rent based on protected characteristics
rules.requirement: Owners, brokers, managing agents and similar persons may not refuse to rent, lease or sell covered housing, or otherwise deny it, because of listed protected characteristics such as race, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, veteran status or handicap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covered housing accommodations and land intended for housing under subsections 10, 11, 12 or 13 of section one
rules.exemptions: Leasing of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as his residence. The term 'age' does not apply to minors or to certain state/federally-aided elderly housing, LIHTC housing, or registered 55+/62+ communities.
rules.interaction: Federal Fair Housing Act (42 USC 3601 et seq.) governs 55+/62+ housing compliance

rules.requirement: Landlords and their agents may not make or cause to be made any written or oral inquiry or keep any record about an applicant's protected characteristics (race, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, handicap, etc.).
rules.coverage_conditions: Other covered housing accommodations and land under subsections 10, 11, 12 or 13 of section one
rules.exemptions: Leasing of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as his residence.

rules.requirement: Handicap discrimination includes refusing to rent to a person because of the person's need for a reasonable modification or accommodation.

rules.exemptions: Accommodations/modifications paid for by the owner need not be provided if they impose an undue hardship.
rules.quoted_span: discrimination against or a refusal to rent to a person because of such person's need for reasonable modification or accommodation

rules.title: Source-of-income / public assistance and housing subsidy discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Persons furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against an individual because the individual receives public assistance or a housing subsidy (including rental assistance), or because of any requirement of such a program.
rules.key_value: No discrimination against public assistance or housing subsidy recipients

rules.quoted_span: to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements

rules.title: Familial status (children) discrimination in housing prohibited
rules.requirement: Owners, brokers, managing agents and others with the right to rent, lease or sell covered housing may not refuse, deny or discriminate in terms, conditions, privileges or services because a person has a child or children who will occupy the premises. rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under written lease; right to cure
rules.requirement: If a tenant under a written lease neglects or refuses to pay rent, the landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can defeat termination by paying or tendering all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the answer day in the landlord's possession action.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit; cure by paying rent due + interest + costs by answer day
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies under a written lease where rent is due and unpaid.

rules.title: Continuance and tenancy reinstatement where nonpayment caused by government payment delay
rules.requirement: If nonpayment was caused by a failure or delay of federal, state or municipal government in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment (other than salary), the court must continue the hearing at least seven days to notify the agency. If all rent, interest and costs are tendered in that time, the court must treat the tenancy as not terminated.
rules.key_value: Minimum 7-day continuance; tenancy treated as not terminated if full payment tendered
rules.coverage_conditions: Nonpayment caused by government failure or delay in mailing/delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher to tenant or landlord.
rules.exemptions: Salary payments are excluded.
rules.interaction: Operates as a protection within the § 11 nonpayment termination process.
rules.quoted_span: the court in any such action shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency

rules.title: Notice to terminate tenancy at will (no-cause termination notice period)
rules.requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with three months' written notice. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than three months, notice must equal the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. The notice may include an offer of a new tenancy on different terms without invalidating the notice.
rules.key_value: 3 months' written notice (or rental period interval/30 days, whichever is longer, if rent is paid at intervals under 3 months)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies at will
rules.interaction: The statute sets only notice timing and does not require a stated cause for ending a tenancy at will; it is not a just-cause requirement.
