rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent and right to cure
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a tenancy at will for nonpayment of rent with 14 days' written notice to quit. A tenant who has not received a similar notice in the previous 12 months can stop termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days of receiving the notice. The notice must include a statutory statement of this right. If it omits the statement, the tenant's cure period extends to the day the answer is due in a possession action.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice to quit; 10-day cure right (once per 12 months)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants at will with unpaid rent. The cure right applies only if the tenant has not received a similar notice in the preceding 12 months.
rules.exemptions: If nonpayment was caused by a delay or failure of a government agency in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment (not salary), the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days. If all rent, interest and costs are tendered in that time, the tenancy is treated as not terminated.

rules.requirement: The executive office of housing and livable communities may authorize by regulation an optional fee in lieu of a security deposit. rules.title: Security deposit remains tenant's property; no commingling
rules.requirement: A security deposit remains the tenant's property, may not be commingled with the lessor's assets, and is not subject to claims of the lessor's creditors, including foreclosing mortgagees or bankruptcy trustees. The tenant is entitled only to interest as provided in subsection (3)(b).
rules.quoted_span: A security deposit shall continue to be the property of the tenant making such deposit, shall not be commingled with the assets of the lessor

rules.title: Interest on last month's rent paid in advance
rules.requirement: A lessor who collects last month's rent in advance must give a detailed receipt and pay the tenant interest at 5% per year (or a lesser amount actually received from the bank), paid annually or within 30 days of termination. Failure to pay interest within 30 days after termination exposes the lessor to treble damages plus costs and attorneys' fees.
rules.key_value: 5% per year interest; 3x damages for nonpayment
rules.quoted_span: pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held.

rules.title: Receipt for security deposit
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent receiving a security deposit must give a signed receipt at the time of receipt stating the amount, recipient's name (and lessor's name if an agent), date, and a description of the premises.
rules.quoted_span: shall give said tenant or prospective tenant at the time of receiving such security deposit a receipt indicating the amount of such security deposit

rules.title: Statement of condition of premises
rules.requirement: A lessor accepting a security deposit must furnish a separate written statement of the premises' condition, listing existing damage and code violations, within ten days after commencement of tenancy or upon receipt of deposit, whichever is later, with a prescribed bold notice. The tenant has fifteen days to return it or submit a separate damage list, and the lessor must respond within fifteen days.
rules.key_value: 10 days to furnish; 15 days for tenant response
rules.quoted_span: furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.

rules.title: Lessor record-keeping for security deposits
rules.requirement: Every lessor accepting a security deposit must maintain records of deposits, damage descriptions, termination dates, repairs and costs, including copies of receipts and statements of condition. Records must be available for tenant inspection during normal business hours.
rules.quoted_span: Every lessor who accepts a security deposit shall maintain a record of all such security deposits received

rules.title: Security deposit must be held in separate interest-bearing account
rules.requirement: Lessor must hold any security deposit in a separate, interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, beyond the claims of the lessor's creditors and transferable to a subsequent owner. A receipt with bank name, location, amount and account number must be given to the tenant within 30 days; failure entitles the tenant to immediate return of the deposit.
rules.key_value: Separate interest-bearing MA bank account; receipt within 30 days
rules.quoted_span: shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: A lessor holding a deposit for one year or longer must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year (or the lesser amount actually received from the bank) at the end of each year, and give an annual statement; accrued interest is due within 30 days if the tenancy ends early. If not received within 30 days after year end, the tenant may deduct the interest from next rent.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser bank interest
rules.coverage_conditions: Deposit held one year or longer from commencement of tenancy
rules.quoted_span: pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after termination of occupancy or end of the lease, the lessor must return the deposit or balance, deducting only for unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax increases under a conforming escalation clause, and reasonable repair of tenant-caused damage excluding normal wear and tear.
rules.key_value: 30 days
rules.quoted_span: return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof

rules.title: Itemized sworn list of damages required for damage deductions
rules.requirement: To deduct for damage, the lessor must provide within 30 days an itemized list of damages sworn under pains and penalties of perjury, with written evidence of actual or estimated repair costs. No deduction for damage listed in the move-in condition statement unless subsequently repaired and renewed damage is proven unrelated.
rules.key_value: Sworn itemized list within 30 days
rules.quoted_span: an itemized list of damages, sworn to by the lessor or his agent under pains and penalties of perjury

rules.title: Deductions limited to statutory purposes
rules.requirement: No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those listed in the statute.
rules.key_value: Only unpaid rent/water, tax increases, tenant-caused damage
rules.quoted_span: No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section.

rules.title: No deduction for damage listed in move-in condition statement
rules.requirement: Lessor may not deduct for damage listed in the separate written statement of condition given before the tenancy or in the tenant's signed list, unless the lessor repaired it and can prove the renewed damage was unrelated and tenant-caused.
rules.quoted_span: No amount shall be deducted from the security deposit for any damage to the dwelling unit which was listed in the separate written statement of the present condition of the premises

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor in interest
rules.requirement: On transfer of the lessor's interest, the deposit and accrued interest must be transferred to the successor, who is liable for it and must notify the tenant in writing within 45 days. A mortgage is not a transfer.
rules.key_value: Notice within 45 days
rules.exemptions: Liability does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty, or a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession that is a state- or federally-chartered financial institution.
rules.quoted_span: the lessor shall transfer such security deposit together with any interest which has accrued thereon for the benefit of the tenant

rules.title: Lessor must maintain record of damages and deposits for two years
rules.requirement: Lessor must keep records of damage, repairs, and receipts or condition statements for each unit with a deposit for two years after tenancy ends, available for tenant inspection; wrongful failure entitles tenant to immediate return of the deposit with interest.
rules.key_value: 2 years
rules.quoted_span: shall maintain said record for each dwelling unit or premises for which a security deposit was accepted for a period of two years

rules.title: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit
rules.requirement: The lessor forfeits the right to retain any portion of the deposit, or to counterclaim for damage, if he fails to deposit funds properly, fails to provide the itemized damage list in 30 days, uses conflicting lease provisions or seeks waivers, fails to transfer the deposit, or fails to return it within 30 days.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall forfeit his right to retain any portion of the security deposit for any reason

rules.title: Treble damages for deposit violations
rules.requirement: For violations of clauses (a), (d) or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant is awarded three times the deposit or balance owed, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 3x deposit + 5% interest + costs and attorney's fees
rules.quoted_span: the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof

rules.title: Successor in interest assumes liability for tenant rental advance and must give notice within 45 days
rules.requirement: When a lessor transfers its interest in the premises, the successor must credit the tenant with the rental advance and pay all accrued interest. The successor must give the tenant written notice within 45 days of the transfer. The notice must include the lessor's and any agent's name, business address and business telephone number. Granting a mortgage is not a transfer.
rules.key_value: Written notice within 45 days of transfer
rules.exemptions: Granting a mortgage is not a transfer of interest.
rules.quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such rental advance that such rental advance was so credited

rules.title: Successor liability where lessor fails to credit rental advance; free occupancy alternative
rules.requirement: If the lessor does not credit the rental advance to its successor, the successor becomes liable to the tenant for crediting it and paying interest, whatever the nature of the transfer. If the tenant still occupies the unit, the successor may satisfy the obligation by giving free use and occupancy for the period the advance covered.
rules.key_value: Free use and occupancy for the period covered by the advance
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies where the lessor fails to credit the rental advance to the successor in interest.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a city or town that acquires title under chapter sixty, or to a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession that is a financial institution chartered by the Commonwealth or the United States.
rules.quoted_span: the successor in interest shall, without regard to the nature of the transfer, assume liability for crediting of the rental advance

rules.title: Lease provisions and tenant waivers of § 15B are void
rules.requirement: Any lease provision that conflicts with § 15B, and any waiver of its provisions by a tenant or prospective tenant, is against public policy and void and unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable

rules.title: Short-term vacation or recreational rentals exempt from § 15B
rules.requirement: Section 15B does not apply to a lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of 100 days or less for a vacation or recreational purpose.
rules.key_value: 100 days or less
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies of 100 days or less used for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less are excluded from § 15B.
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of this section shall not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which lease or rental is for a vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection: presumption against termination or rent increase within six months of protected tenant activity
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, or organizing or joining a tenants' union. A termination-of-tenancy notice (other than for nonpayment), a rent increase, or a substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal. The presumption is rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence. Violators are liable for 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater), plus costs and attorney's fees. Lease waivers are void.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal; damages of 1–3 months' rent or actual damages, plus attorney's fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential premises tenants who commenced or obtained relief in housing-law actions, reported code violations, or organized or joined a tenants' union
rules.exemptions: Notices of termination for nonpayment of rent are excluded from the presumption
rules.interaction: Waiver of this section in any lease or rental agreement is void and unenforceable. This is an anti-retaliation rule, not a general just-cause eviction requirement.
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment must be accompanied by state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given to a residential tenant must be accompanied by a form documenting any repayment agreements and providing information on rental assistance programs, court rules/orders on summary process, and relevant federal or state eviction restrictions. The form must prominently state that the notice is not an eviction, the tenant need not leave immediately, and only a court order can force the tenant to leave.
rules.key_value: Mandatory form accompanying notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Written notices to quit for nonpayment of rent given by a landlord to a residential tenant under chapter 186
rules.interaction: Form is developed by the executive office of housing and livable communities; information in subsection (a)(ii) must be available in the 5 most common languages in the commonwealth in addition to English.
rules.quoted_span: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form

rules.title: Courts may not accept nonpayment eviction filings without proof of form delivery
rules.requirement: No court with jurisdiction over summary process actions under chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, may accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint in a nonpayment eviction for a residential unit without proof of delivery of the required form.
rules.key_value: Proof of delivery of form required for filing
rules.coverage_conditions: Summary process actions under chapter 239 for nonpayment of rent for residential dwelling units
rules.interaction: Enforces the notice-form requirement in § 31(a) at the court filing stage.
rules.quoted_span: accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: no advertising or records that unlawfully limit based on criminal record
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not publish, post, or mail any statement, advertisement, or sign, or use any application form or make any record or inquiry, that directly or indirectly expresses an unlawful limitation or discrimination based on criminal record. Exceptions apply as permitted by the act, for methamphetamine manufacture convictions on federally assisted housing premises, and for lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record limitations in ads, applications, or inquiries
rules.exemptions: Drug-related criminal activity for manufacture or production of methamphetamine on premises of federally assisted housing; lifetime sex offender registration requirement under a State program; other matters permitted by the act.
rules.quoted_span: shall not print, publish, circulate, issue, display, post, or mail, or cause to

rules.title: Limits on dissemination and use of applicant criminal record
rules.requirement: Unless otherwise required by law, a housing provider may not share an applicant's criminal record with anyone not expected to use it to evaluate the applicant consistently with the act, and may not use it for any purpose inconsistent with the act.
rules.exemptions: Where otherwise required by law
rules.quoted_span: disseminate an applicant’s criminal record to any person who is not expected to

rules.title: Landlord immunity for renting to individuals with criminal records
rules.requirement: Landlords covered by the act are immune from civil liability arising from a decision to rent to individuals with a criminal record or from a decision not to conduct a criminal background screening. Existing immunity for renting to persons convicted of specified serious offenses is unaffected.
rules.key_value: Civil immunity
rules.quoted_span: housing opportunities to formerly incarcerated individuals, landlords subject

rules.title: Ban on required drug or alcohol tests and drug treatment information
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant's consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.key_value: No drug/alcohol testing of applicants
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant

rules.title: Administrative enforcement and tiered penalties under Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Violations are enforced administratively through the Division, not by court action. Penalties are up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 with one other violation in five years, and up to $10,000 with two or more other violations in seven years.
rules.key_value: $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000 tiered penalties
rules.exemptions: Housing provider avoids penalty if complaint is addressed through the 14-day mediation process.
rules.interaction: Does not bar independent rights or actions, including under the Law Against Discrimination (P.L.1945, c.169).
rules.quoted_span: an amount not to exceed $1,000 if the housing

rules.title: Director may order return of rental application fee for violations
rules.requirement: Unless housing is provided to the applicant as a remedy, the director may require that the applicant's rental application fee be returned, and may require up to $1,000 of the penalty to be paid to the applicant.
rules.key_value: Application fee refund; up to $1,000 to applicant
rules.exemptions: Not applicable if housing is provided to the applicant under paragraph (2)
rules.quoted_span: applicant’s rental application fee be returned; and

rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50 (CPI-adjusted annually). The Division of Consumer Affairs must adopt implementing rules, including a mechanism for reporting violations.
rules.key_value: $50 maximum application fee
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property leased or subleased for dwelling purposes (other than one- and two-family dwellings).
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply

rules.title: Penalties for excessive application fees
rules.requirement: Violators are liable for penalties of up to $500 (first offense), $750 (second), and $1,000 (each subsequent), enforced by summary proceedings in Special Civil Part on complaint of the Director of Consumer Affairs or Attorney General. The amount wrongfully charged is taken from the penalty and remitted to the applicant.
rules.key_value: Up to $500 / $750 / $1,000 per offense
rules.coverage_conditions: Same as application fee cap.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one- or two-family dwellings; non-landlord NJ Real Estate Commission licensees.
rules.quoted_span: shall be liable for a penalty of up to $500 for a first offense

rules.title: Annual CPI adjustment of application fee cap
rules.requirement: Each January 1 following enactment, the $50 fee limit is adjusted by the Director of Consumer Affairs in proportion to the percent change in the NY-Northern NJ-Long Island CPI-U over the 12 months ending October 31, only if the change is greater than zero. The Director publishes the limit annually on the Division's website.
rules.key_value: $50 adjusted annually by CPI change (if positive)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the application fee limit under subsection a.
rules.quoted_span: made only if the percent change in the Consumer Price Index for the period

rules.title: Good cause required for lease non-renewal (Anti-Eviction Act)
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential rental properties may not refuse to renew any lease, written or oral, unless they have good cause under the Anti-Eviction Act. The statutory good causes are listed in the Eviction section of the guide.
rules.key_value: Good cause required to non-renew
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties generally
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units (owner-occupied 2-3 family buildings are covered by separate rules).
rules.interaction: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are addressed in a separate section of the guide.
rules.quoted_span: regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease

rules.title: Pet-related grounds for non-renewal in senior citizen housing projects
rules.requirement: In senior citizen housing projects, a landlord may refuse to renew a lease because of a pet only in limited circumstances. These include code violations by the pet, failure to care for or control the pet, and failure to keep pet waste from interfering with common areas.
rules.key_value: Four enumerated pet-related non-renewal grounds
rules.coverage_conditions: Senior citizen housing project: any building or structure with three or more rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than three rental dwelling units; health care facilities.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant fails to properly care for the pet;

rules.title: No eviction merely because lease term has ended
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a lease only by offering a new lease with different terms (e.g., higher rent or new rules) that the tenant does not accept. A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended; termination is distinct from eviction.
rules.key_value: Lease expiration alone is not grounds for eviction
rules.interaction: Statutory citation not stated in this excerpt; refers to the eviction section of the publication for more detail.
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq. (Anti-Eviction Act), as summarized by NJ DCA Tenant Information publication
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.

rules.title: Security deposit return after domestic violence lease termination (Safe Housing Act)
rules.requirement: A tenant who terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act is entitled to return of the security deposit plus interest. Within 3 business days after termination the landlord must give written notice of when and where the deposit can be picked up (copy to the relocation officer or municipal clerk), and within 15 business days must make the deposit available with an itemized list of interest and deductions. Deposit must remain available for 30 days, after which unclaimed funds are redeposited or reinvested per the Security Deposit law. The landlord may deduct amounts due under the lease, including damage beyond ordinary wear and tear and unpaid rent.
rules.key_value: Notice within 3 business days; return within 15 business days; available 30 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants terminating before lease expiration under the NJ Safe Housing Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.4 et seq.)
rules.exemptions: Law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.interaction: Operates in accordance with the general NJ Security Deposit law.
rules.quoted_span: the tenant is entitled to the return of their security deposit

rules.title: Security deposit return after SCRA lease termination
rules.requirement: When a service member terminates a lease under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, the landlord must return the security deposit in accordance with the NJ Security Deposit Law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Service members terminating a lease under the SCRA with written notice and copy of military orders
rules.interaction: Incorporates the general NJ Security Deposit Law.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is required to return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law

rules.title: Security deposit cap of 1.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent. Prepaid funds held to secure future rents (including last month's rent) count toward the cap, and a pet deposit combined with the regular deposit cannot exceed the cap.
rules.key_value: 1.5 x monthly rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in by written request; applies 30 days after request).
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent

rules.title: Annual security deposit increase limited to 10%
rules.requirement: Any additional yearly increase in the security deposit may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 10% of current deposit per year
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling unless tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Maximum move-in payment of 2.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: At lease inception a landlord may require only the security deposit (up to 1.5 months' rent) plus first month's rent, totaling no more than 2.5 times monthly rent.
rules.key_value: 2.5 x monthly rent at inception
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling unless tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: the landlo rd may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease

rules.title: Security deposit held in trust, interest-bearing account
rules.requirement: Security deposits remain the tenant's property, held in trust and not commingled with the landlord's assets. Landlords with fewer than 10 units must deposit in an interest-bearing account at an insured New Jersey bank; larger landlords have additional investment options.
rules.key_value: Held in trust; interest-bearing account
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties; ten or fewer units vs. 10 or more units rules differ.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling unless tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: The security deposit shall not be comingled with the personal property or become an asset of the landlord.

rules.title: No statewide rent control; municipalities may enact rent control
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide law capping or controlling rents. Municipalities may adopt local rent control or rent leveling ordinances, enforced by local boards.
rules.key_value: No state cap; local option
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies where a municipality has enacted a rent control or rent leveling ordinance
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings (30 years); rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt
rules.citation: NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant Information (Rent Control/Rent Increases)
rules.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years after completion of construction. Government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
rules.key_value: 30-year exemption from local rent control
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, 30 years following completion of construction
rules.exemptions: Subsidized rents may also be exempt
rules.interaction: Limits the reach of municipal rent control ordinances

rules.title: No mid-lease rent increase; lease termination and notice required

rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act

rules.title: Notice to quit and notice of rent increase before eviction for nonpayment of increased rent

rules.key_value: Notice to quit + notice of rent increase
rules.quoted_span: before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.

rules.title: Reasonable rental application fees and screening report costs permitted
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge the tenant the cost of a credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees. No specific dollar cap is stated in this text.
rules.key_value: Reasonable application fees; cost of report
rules.citation: NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant Information (Credit Checks and Background Checks)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.

rules.title: Adverse action notice when application denied due to credit report
rules.requirement: If an application is denied because of a credit report, the landlord must give the applicant the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or screening agency that supplied the report (federal FCRA requirement).
rules.key_value: Adverse action notice with agency contact information
rules.coverage_conditions: Denial based on a credit report from a credit bureau or screening agency
rules.quoted_span: provide the tenant with the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable and require valid notice
rules.requirement: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent control ordinance.
rules.key_value: No unconscionable increases; valid notice required
rules.coverage_conditions: Statewide; unconscionability is fact-sensitive (amount of increase, landlord expenses and profitability, comparable rents, bargaining position).
rules.exemptions: HUD-owned/subsidized housing and NJHMFA-controlled rents are not subject to municipal rent control.

The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: No rent increase to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still be raised to cover new services or amenities.
rules.key_value: No increase for conversion-only costs
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of units; applies to all tenants regardless of senior/disabled protected tenancy status.
rules.quoted_span: rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion

rules.title: Lease termination with new lease at increased rent; notice requirements
rules.requirement: To terminate a lease and offer a new lease at increased rent, the landlord must give proper written notice that the current lease is terminated and that the tenant may remain by signing a new lease at an increased rent.
rules.quoted_span:
Landlord must give the tenant proper written notice, which informs the tenant that the current 
lease is terminated, and the tenant can remain in the premises by signing a new lease at an 
increased rent.

rules.title: Landlord registration required to evict
rules.requirement: A landlord who has not properly registered cannot evict a tenant in the building. In an eviction action by a non-compliant landlord, the court must continue the case up to 90 days to allow compliance, then dismiss if the landlord has not complied.
rules.key_value: Up to 90 days to cure before dismissal
rules.coverage_conditions: One or two-family non-owner-occupied homes (file with municipal clerk); buildings with 3+ units (file with Bureau of Housing Inspection).

The landlord 
registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act – Good Cause Required for Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, and must prove the grounds in court. Possession may be recovered only by consent or through legal eviction process.
rules.key_value: Good cause required for eviction and lease non-renewal

rules.exemptions: May not apply to owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: NJ Notice to Quit / Notice to Cease Requirements for Good Cause Evictions
rules.requirement: Each good cause ground other than nonpayment must be described in detail in a written notice. A Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent, and a Notice to Cease may also be required, with a reasonable compliance period. A Judgment for Possession is required before the tenant must move.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit required (except nonpayment); Notice to Cease reasonable period
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act
rules.exemptions: Nonpayment of rent evictions do not require a Notice to Quit; owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units and transient/seasonal guests are excluded from the Act.
rules.quoted_span:
